coverage_interpretation: Depth-reference coverage includes source-selected inverse-transport sections and core context. It does not imply complete lower boundaries, full thickness fields, seasonal envelopes or volumes. Cruise/decade groups remain distinct. Local zero-flow boundaries from a processed climatology do not establish instantaneous or whole-route thickness. An upper-component depth reference does not cover the deep component; independent sections do not inherit unrelated width observations. Strict upper bounds are not point estimates. Overlapping mooring studies and model/observational cases remain distinct, without constructing numerical uncertainty or annual ranges. Deep domains with unspecified seafloor endpoints do not establish numerical thickness; spatially distinct summaries and current components remain separate. Source-reported regional thickness is distinct from bottom or core depth and is not a whole-route thickness field. Core operators and branch definitions remain explicit. Inclusive lower bounds preserve at-least statements. Thermohaline and velocity cores remain separately defined; named jets do not fill other families or basin identities. Regional variation within one campaign is not seasonal extrema. Winter-branch reach remains partial, and current-meander layer thickness is distinct from developed eddy extent. Seasonal model directions retain their separate sections and simulation time basis. Direction reversal is distinct from transport integration limits; regional mean core bands and observed section bands are not temporal extrema. Ranges of reach scales, depth bands across property cores and selected stream-tube domains remain distinct. Partial named branches and source reconstruction methods are explicit. Branch reach retains partial spatial scope. Instrument-limited reach and current-classification conventions are not detected physical bottoms. Mooring array means retain their own longitude and averaging months. Partial strait cores retain mean-profile years separately from observing-record span. Net section transport zero depths retain section-specific lateral selection and are not pointwise flow boundaries. Local directional-layer crossings retain profile coordinates, sampling interval and pinned operator; they are not unique physical named-current boundaries. Component depth bands retain their water mass. Seasonal parent-system context is distinct from segment profiles. Author isotach boundaries retain reference levels and section support. Qualitative near-halt depth does not establish exact zero or a full-flow bottom. Pacific system branches retain distinct depth definitions and six alongshore undercurrent sections. Model years are simulation indices. Observed inclusive reach and seasonal confinement bounds do not establish complete current bottoms. Local monthly maxima retain shallow sampling censoring, record gaps and short-record caveats. Branch reach bounds and observation-supported approximate extent do not establish exact route-wide boundaries. Indian Ocean references distinguish regional geostrophic reach, transport integration depth and a source-reported scale distance. Distinct SICC/SECC identities and historical WAC naming do not authorize whole-route depth inheritance. Regional water-mass depth is distinct from a kinematic boundary. BSO core uses salinity ranking. Conditional Davidson northern context is ineligible for projection along the catalog reference route. Dominant-flow layer extent retains an unquantified fraction and assumed geostrophic reference. Multicruise support is not continuous. Portugal subpolar ENACW is component evidence in a modern setting, distinct from adjacent Azores water and the paleorecord.
